name: Pat Stryker
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2001-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026); Wikidata (2025)
forbes_bio: Pat Stryker is a philanthropist and the founder of Bohemian Foundation, which supports music, community, global and civic programs.
The healthcare heir has given $225 million to charity over her lifetime, primarily through the foundation.
Her grandfather founded Stryker Corp., which sold $18.4 billion worth of medical equipment in 2022.
In 2016, she and her brother, Jon Stryker, gave a combined $10 million to fund the nation's first memorial to the victims of racial terror lynchings.
forbes_facts: Stryker lives in Fort Collins, Colorado, where she has been redeveloping downtown real estate.
Stryker is a big donor to Colorado State University and to Democratic political campaigns.

name: Cameron Adams
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2022-2025); Hurun Global (2023-2026); Hurun Unicorn founders (2019-2024)
forbes_bio: Cameron Adams is cofounder and chief product officer of design software maker Canva, which was valued by private investors at $42 billion in August 2025.
An ex-Googler who had founded his own startup in Sydney, Australia, Adams was recruited by Melanie Perkins and Cliff Obrecht to be an advisor for Canva.
Instead, Adams signed on as the startup's third cofounder in June 2012. He leads technical development for the company.
Canva's software enables the creation of visuals for things like menus, resumes and Instagram graphics.

name: John Fisher
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2001-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026); SEC insider holdings (2025-2026)
forbes_bio: John Fisher is the youngest of Gap founders Doris and Donald Fisher's three sons.
He stepped down from Gap's board of directors in May 2022. His brothers Robert and William still sit on the board.
John is a founding partner of investment firm Sansome Partners and sits on the board of the Silicon Schools Fund.
He is a majority owner of the Oakland A's baseball team and has smaller stakes in MLS' San Jose Earthquakes and the Scottish Glasgow Celtic F.C.
forbes_facts: The three Fisher brothers attended Princeton University and went on to study at Stanford University's School of Business.
John is a chairman of the Knowledge Is Power Program Foundation (KIPP), a non-profit network of public charter schools.

name: Patrice Motsepe
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2008-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026)
forbes_bio: Patrice Motsepe, the founder and chairman of African Rainbow Minerals, became a billionaire in 2008 - the first black African on the Forbes list.
In 2016, he launched a private equity firm, African Rainbow Capital, focused on investing in Africa.
Motsepe also has a stake in Sanlam, a listed financial services firm, and is the president and owner of the Mamelodi Sundowns Football Club.
In March 2021, Motsepe was elected president of the Confederation of African Football, the sport's governing body on the continent.
In 1994, he became the first black partner at law firm Bowman Gilfillan in Johannesburg, and then started a mining services contracting business.
In 1997, he bought low-producing gold mine shafts and later turned them profitable.
forbes_facts: In 2013, the mining magnate was the first African to sign Bill Gates' and Warren Buffett's Giving Pledge, promising to give at least half his fortune to charity.
Motsepe benefited from South Africa's Black Economic Empowerment (BEE) laws, mandating that companies be at least 26% black-owned to get a government mining license.

name: Tim Cook
sec_insider_companies: Apple Inc. (AAPL) - Chief Executive Officer; NIKE, Inc. (NKE) - Director
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2021-2025); Hurun Global (2021-2026); Wikidata (2026); SEC insider holdings (2026)
forbes_bio: Tim Cook is the CEO of Apple, one of the world's most valuable companies.
Cook, who became chief executive in 2011, had previously served as Apple's chief operating officer under Steve Jobs.
Cook joined Apple in 1998, having worked briefly at PC-maker Compaq and for 12 years at IBM.
Cook owns more than 3 million shares of Apple, less than a 1% stake; he's sold more than $1 billion worth of shares over the years.
Since 2005, he has also served on the board of Nike.
forbes_facts: Cook also sits on the board of trustees of Duke, where he got his MBA in 1988.
Originally from Alabama, Cook hails from humble roots: His father was a shipyard worker and his mother worked at a pharmacy.

name: Amy Goldman Fowler
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2026); Forbes annual (2017-2025); Hurun Global (2020-2026)
forbes_bio: Real estate heiress Amy Goldman Fowler is one of four siblings who equally split ownership of Solil Management, which owns 400 properties.
Amy is the second-youngest daughter of late patriarch Sol Goldman. His trademark was all-cash deals whenever possible.
She worked in the real estate office when she was younger. Now her younger sister Jane runs it.
She lives on a 200-acre farm in Rhinebeck, New York and also has a home in Memphis.
Amy has a Ph.D. in clinical psychology and has won three American Horticultural Society book awards.
forbes_facts: Her husband Dr. Cary Fowler helped start the climate change conscious Svalbard Global Seed Vault.
She is an author; her latest book was The Melon, published in 2019, with photographs and descriptions of 125 different melon varieties.

name: J. Hyatt Brown
sec_insider_companies: BROWN & BROWN, INC. (BRO) - President and CEO
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2018-2025); Hurun Global (2019-2026); SEC insider holdings (2026)
forbes_bio: J. Hyatt Brown chairs New York Stock Exchange-traded Brown & Brown, the fourth largest insurance brokerage in the U.S.
His father, J. Adrian Brown, cofounded the company in Daytona Beach in 1939, and Hyatt became CEO in 1961.
Under Hyatt, Brown & Brown grew from a local, family-owned business into a firm with over 15,000 employees and 500 locations worldwide.
Hyatt's son J. Powell Brown took over as CEO in 2009; the elder Brown remains chairman.
J. Hyatt Brown owns 15% of Brown & Brown, which trades on the New York stock exchange.
forbes_facts: Brown was elected to the Florida House of Representatives in 1972 and served as the Speaker of the House in Florida from 1978 to 1980.
The Cici and Hyatt Brown museum in Daytona Beach, Florida, is home to the largest collection of Florida art in the world.

name: Ugo Gussalli Beretta
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2024-2025); Hurun Global (2025-2026)
forbes_bio: Ugo Gussalli Beretta and his two sons, Pietro and Franco, lead Beretta Holding, the world's oldest firearms manufacturer founded in Italy in 1526.
They are the 14th and 15th generations to lead the company, whose first deal was the sale of 185 arquebus barrels to the Republic of Venice in 1526.
Ugo stepped down from executive positions in 2015 and sits on the board of Luxembourg-based Beretta Holding, which is headed by Pietro, who created the holding company.
Franco leads subsidiary Fabbrica d'Armi Pietro Beretta, which still owns factories in the town of Gardone Val Trompia, where the company was founded.

name: James Dinan
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2008-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026)
forbes_bio: James Dinan founded York Capital Management in 1991 and is the former chairman and CEO of the money management firm.
York Capital had $1.6 billion of assets under management as of March 2025, down from $19 billion in 2019.
In 2014 Dinan purchased a minority stake in the NBA's Milwaukee Bucks, alongside fellow finance tycoons Marc Lasry and Wes Edens.
Dinan obtained his B.S. degree in economics from the Wharton School and his M.B.A from Harvard Business School.
Dinan, who stopped serving as chairman of York Capital in late 2023, now spends his time managing his family office, according to a filing from York Capital.
forbes_facts: Dinan lost much of his savings in the 1987 Black Monday stock market crash. Four years later, he founded York Capital Management.
Dinan sits on numerous boards, including that of the Lincoln Center for the Performing Arts and the Museum of the City of New York.

name: Liying Chen
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2022-2023); Forbes annual (2017-2023); Hurun Global (2017-2026); Hurun China (2016-2026); Hurun Self-Made Women (2017-2020)
forbes_bio: Chen Liying cofounded Yunda Express, one of China's biggest logistics companies, in Shanghai in 1999.
Yunda Express went public through a reverse merger on the Shenzhen Stock Exchange in December 2016.
Chen owns roughly 21% of the listed company Yunda Holding, and serves as vice chairman.
Husband Nie Tengyun is a fellow billionaire and chairman of Yunda Holding.

name: Nicholas Pritzker II
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2019); Forbes annual (2010-2018)
forbes_bio: Nicholas (Nick) Pritzker, II is a cousin of the late Jay Pritzker and his brothers Donald and Robert, who built the Hyatt hotel chain.
Pritzker spent many years leading Hyatt's new hotel development efforts but he has since sold most of his Hyatt stock.
He has shifted his attention and investment dollars to causes like clean energy, marijuana legalization and criminal justice reform.
He cofounded and cochairs Clean Energy Trust, which invests in clean energy companies in the Midwest.
Nick was an early investor in the e-cigarette maker Juul and the synthetic DNA company Twist Biosciences through his investment firm, Tao Capital.
forbes_facts: In the 2016 election, Pritzker donated to Proposition 64, a ballot initiative in California which successfully legalized marijuana in the Golden State.

Zhang holds degrees from Sichuan University and the China Europe International Business School.

name: Alexander Nesis
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2024); Forbes annual (2010-2023); Hurun Global (2014-2022)
forbes_bio: Alexander Nesis is founder of precious mining firm Polymetal International and private equity firm ICT Group.
His brother Vitaly is CEO of Polymetal, in which BlackRock also has a stake greater than 10%.
ICT, through which he owns his Polymetal stake, announced in March 2022 Nesis' stake was just under 50%, less than previously thought. He reduced it to avoid the risk of sanctions for the company.
ICT has stakes in Polymetal and railcar maker United Wagon.
Nesis got his start in the late 1980s using uranium production waste from a mine in Uzbekistan to produce and sell rare-earth metals.
forbes_facts: He is now a Swiss resident with citizenship of Israel, Malta and Russia.
